title: Hof restore plan
description: hofctl restore's own deterministic plan contract (ADR 0006) - always against a SECOND, genuinely clean target instance, never the same host a backup was taken from (that is in-place restore, item 11's own later scope). target below is the new host's own freshly-observed binding; source below is the historical installation being restored onto it - the two are never conflated, and installationId/generation are restored verbatim from source, never incremented.

planId.description: sha256 of this plan's own entire content minus planId itself (scripts/backup-ids.mjs's canonicalContentId) - target binding, cleanObservation, source, snapshotId, manifestDigest, consistencySet, networks all included, deterministic, never a timestamp. Pins not just WHICH backup this restore approves but WHAT will actually be restored (via snapshotId/manifestDigest) and that the target was actually observed clean (via cleanObservation), not merely claimed to be.

executable.description: false when blockers is non-empty (target not genuinely clean, snapshot/manifest/release-lock verification failed, another operation already in progress, ...).

target.description: The NEW, clean target this restore will run against - its own freshly-observed host key, re-checked once more under the mutex before any restore operation is dispatched (never trusted from planning time alone).

cleanObservation.description: What target.verify-clean actually found, at planning time, on the new target - structural proof of "genuinely clean" beyond target.installationId being null and target.baselineGeneration being 0 (which a caller could otherwise supply without any real observation behind them). Every list is required to be empty: a target-verify-clean.mjs a later PR writes populates these from a real observation and this plan is only ever built, and only ever approved, when every one of them came back empty. Re-checked once more under the mutex at target.verify-clean dispatch time, exactly like the host key above - never trusted from planning time alone either.

destinationName.description: Which of the historical backup's own configured destinations this snapshot is being read from.

snapshotId.description: The exact restic snapshot id this plan pins at APPROVAL time (snapshot.verify resolved and verified it before the plan was ever built) - never re-resolved from backupId+destinationName again at dispatch time. Without this, an operator approving a plan by backupId+destinationName alone would be approving whatever the repository happens to contain at EXECUTION time, not what they actually reviewed - a repository's contents are not otherwise pinned by planId the way every other approved-then-dispatched document in this repo already is.

manifestDigest.description: sha256 of the exact backup-manifest-v1 document embedded in that same pinned snapshot, verified at planning time - pins WHAT this restore will actually recreate (the consistencySet, the release, the generation) as firmly as snapshotId pins WHICH snapshot, so a manifest that could theoretically differ from what was reviewed at approval time is never silently substituted at dispatch time either.

source.description: The historical installation this backup was taken from - kept distinct from target's own identity for the whole lifetime of this plan and the operation it produces.

releaseLockDigest.description: The historical release lock's own digest, verified against its own original Cosign signature identity - a release lock from an older platform release, restored onto a target running today's tooling, must still verify against exactly the identity it was originally signed with.

recoveryKitDigest.description: sha256 of the recovery kit used for this restore (the encrypted recovery copy of application/TLS/backup secrets, plus the recovery age identity that decrypts it) - never the kit's own decrypted content.

backupToolLockDigest.description: The signed backup-tool-lock this plan was verified against, and whose pinned runner/restic/sops/age binaries this restore actually uses.

consistencySet.description: Same shape as backup-plan-v1's own consistencySet (copied, not $ref'd) - every volume this restore must recreate and repopulate together for a coherent result.

networks.description: Every network this restore's own network.create operations must create before any volume.create or data.restore runs - a clean target has none of Hof's usual infrastructure yet, unlike a plain apply, where the shared network is long-lived, externally-provisioned infrastructure the Ansible network role owns and Compose/plan-v2 never creates. Restore is the one flow that must actually create it, matching ADR 0006's own "operation-owned volumes and networks only" - it never adopts a pre-existing network either, exactly like it never adopts a pre-existing volume. Each entry names the network's own PHYSICAL name (render-topology.mjs's own physicalNetworkName() output, e.g. "hof-hof" - state-v1.schema.json's own committed networks and plan-v2's own desired.networks/network.ensure already use this same physical name, never the bare logical Compose key; recording the logical key here would make this document inconsistent with every other network-naming contract in this repo) and whether it must be created with no default route to the outside world (plan.mjs's own network.ensure carries the identical internal flag for exactly one network, WACHTER_INTERNAL_NETWORK_NAME - "hof-wachter-internal" - restore must recreate that exact property, not merely the network's existence).

allOf.description: executable must faithfully reflect blockers - never a silent mismatch between the two. A plan with any blocker can never claim to be executable, and a plan with none must.
An executable plan always has at least one operation to dispatch - a plan claiming executable: true with an empty operations list is never legitimate.

destinationName.description: Exactly services-v1alpha1.schema.json's own $defs/name pattern (hyphens only, max 63 chars, no dots) - see backup-plan-v1.schema.json's own identical $def for why.

network.description: A network's own PHYSICAL name (render-topology.mjs's own physicalNetworkName() output) plus whether it must be created internal - the same shape plan-v2's own network.ensure operation implicitly carries (name + a conditional internal flag), made explicit here since restore has no baseline to diff against. render-topology.mjs calls physicalNetworkName() exactly twice, ever - HOF_NETWORK_NAME ("hof-hof") and WACHTER_INTERNAL_NETWORK_NAME ("hof-wachter-internal") are the ONLY two physical networks that exist anywhere in this platform, a closed set, not merely a naming convention. A fourth review round tightened name from an unconstrained identifier to a "hof-" prefix pattern, closing the specific {name: "hof", ...} counterexample it found - a fifth round found that pattern still accepted any other "hof-something", e.g. "hof-unrelated", never actually producible by this system. name is now the closed enum itself.

allOf.description: Only hof-wachter-internal (WACHTER_INTERNAL_NETWORK_NAME) is ever internal - render-topology.mjs's own physicalNetworkName("wachter-internal") - every other physical network is external.

installationId.description: The NEW target's own installationId - always null at plan time (a genuinely clean host has none yet); state.restore is what actually assigns source.installationId to it.

baselineGeneration.description: Always 0 - a restore target is required to be genuinely clean, never a host with any prior Hof state of its own.

operation.description: The Restore Flow's own fixed, typed operation whitelist (ADR 0006) - no generic executor. Dispatched in list order, under the shared execution mutex, against the new target only.

resource.description: The network, unit, volume, or fixed checkpoint/config label this operation concerns, depending on action.

condition.description: Only for readiness.wait - reuses plan-v2's own running/healthy vocabulary.

allOf.description: phase and action are a fixed 1:1 mapping - never an inconsistent combination.
